_ruling: A test was written to match the code. I do not care AT ALL about code coverage. The ONLY thing tests should be validating is the requirements. If we are making up tests for coverage that do not map onto requirements then either (a) we are wasting time, or (b) we have identified a new acceptance criteria and we need to retro as to why it wasn't discovered earlier. (human, 2026-08-02)
_mode_why: RATCHET, not enforce. The honest first measurement is 1801 untagged cases of 2728 and 22 authored preconditions. Enforcing would turn trunk red on day one for work nobody has triaged, and a gate that is red for everything is a gate everyone learns to ignore — which is exactly how `make render-diagrams` sat red on trunk for 20 days. So the committed baseline is the floor and it may ONLY SHRINK: a NEW violation blocks, the existing debt is reported every run until the retro decides, per the ruling, whether each is waste or an undiscovered acceptance criterion.
_fileHeaderCoversCounts_why: A file-level `@covers AC-x` is a coverage claim about the MODULE; the ruling asks what THIS CASE validates. Kept strict, and the number it costs is reported separately as `file-header-only` (606 of the 1801) so the retro can see the price of the strictness and change this flag if it disagrees.

roots.why: The product test corpus — app, fids-app, admin-app, adapters, integration and e2e. Both limbs apply.
Cross-project agent-ops tooling. Both limbs are scanned; the limb-1 exemption is taken as a VISIBLE allowlist entry rather than by silently omitting the limb here.

The work-item machinery (python). Limb 1 does not apply: limb-1 parsing is JS/TS only, and these are machinery invariant tests with no product acceptance criterion. Limb 2's exec-boundary rule DOES apply, and this is where founding-evidence instance 2 lived.

derived._why: Fields the FOLD derives from the event-TYPE progression. Hand-setting one builds a prior no real stream can hold - which is precisely how the born-cancelled suppression guard stayed green while nine real prod flights could never heal (UC-HF041, 4e76014). `withdrawn` joins the list with delta-061/DEFECT-OAG-063: it is set ONLY by the presence of a literal OagFlightWithdrawn event type and by NO delta leaf, so a test that hand-sets it has authored a stream reality cannot produce - and the fact it asserts, that a leg's lifecycle ENDED, is exactly the kind a consumer strikes a row on.

allowlist.why: Agent-system MACHINERY invariant tests. They assert a tool's own contract (impacted-tests' node->spec lookup; this gate's own rules) and there is no product acceptance criterion for them to name — the requirement they serve is a PROCESS obligation, not a customer one. Limb 2 still applies to them in full.

_baseline_why: Measured 2026-08-02 at the first run, honestly and without mass-tagging. `ac` = 1801 test cases with no AC reference in their own title, their suite, or their comments, out of 2728 scanned (66%); 606 of the 1801 carry a file-level @covers AC and nothing per-case. `authored` = 22 static hits across 9 files, read one by one at the first run with zero known false positives remaining (three were found and removed by tightening the rules: a runaway destructuring regex, an `expect(...)` argument, and a fixture embedded in a template literal). The ratchet refuses to write a HIGHER number (`--write-baseline` exits 2 unless --allow-baseline-growth), so these two integers can only fall. 1801 -> 1773 by earlier work; 1773 -> 1766 at DEFECT-OAG-068 (2026-08-07), NOT by mass-tagging (EXP-124 says that is a failed experiment and reproduces the coverage theatre the ruling rejects) but because seven existing cases were RETITLED to name the acceptance criterion they were already validating while their subject was being rewritten — e.g. the adapter suite's `if onEvent REJECTS, NO checkpoint` case, which had been green for the life of the service while asserting a precondition that could never hold. The 31 cases added by that defect all name an AC, so they cost nothing here. 1766 -> 1755 at OI-FIDS-INTEGRATION-TIMEOUT (2026-08-07), again not by mass-tagging: the FIDS live-integration tier had been UNRUNNABLE (its beforeAll walked 23,057 sequential feed pages and always timed out), and its eleven cases said `AC1.1`/`AC2.*` — a legacy form the gate's `AC-<ID>.<n>` vocabulary cannot see. Making the tier run in 7s meant reading every case, so each was retitled to the canonical form it already validated, and the two invariants they silently leaned on were registered as real criteria (AC-2.5 the `state` derivation, AC-2.6 the displayed-status parity). Worth noting for the retro: an unrunnable tier freezes its assertions at whatever they said when it last executed, so its criteria age out from under every subsequent defect fix — the limb-1 count cannot distinguish a tagged case that RUNS from a tagged case that cannot. 1755 -> 1749 by the same route, then the ratchet and the tree DIVERGED: DEFECT-OAG-110's keyless-identity work landed 64 untagged cases and 10 authored preconditions ninety minutes after the floor was lowered, and the session that would have run the next gate was lost to an outage, so the first run after those commits was three days later at 1811/25 (DEFECT-OAG-122). 1811 -> 1747 and 25 -> 15 by fixing that item, again not by mass-tagging: every one of the 64 cases was read and retitled to the delta-071 condition it already validated (registered on the item as AC-110.A1-A17 / AC-110.F1-F6), and FOUR criteria those cases had always validated turned out to be unwritten anywhere and were registered as real ACs -- AC-110.9 the route-divergence authority for a keyless stream, AC-110.10 the streamIdDerivation version carrier, AC-110.11 the seam's unchanged keyed branch, AC-110.12 that the census is TOTAL. Of the 10 authored preconditions ONE was a gate false positive (an ARRAY spread read as an object override, fixed in the tool with its own test) and NINE were real: replaced by measurement over the real corpus where reality could settle the claim, and by DECLARED SYNTHETICS whose populations are asserted absent from every capture we hold where it could not. MEASURED RECALL GAP, left open deliberately: `fixturePathTokens` does not match the `fixtures-real/` capture tree, so a whole class of real captures is invisible to the taint walk -- adding that token reveals 22 FURTHER authored preconditions in 8 files (uc-xc5 fan-out replay, the uc-xa3/xa4/xc2/xd2 integration tiers, audit-scheduled-departure-time). Widening it today would push limb 2 to 37 and block every pull, so it is registered as debt rather than taken silently. 1737 -> 1715 at DEFECT-OAG-106 (2026-08-27), and this one is NOT a debt payment at all -- it is the floor being CORRECTED, which is worth distinguishing because the two look identical in this integer. TWENTY-TWO of the 1737 were never test cases: they were Playwright DIRECTIVES. `test.skip(cond, reason)` and a bare `test.skip()` are runtime GUARDS, and the parser admitted `.skip` and classified every match as a case, so a guard was reported as an untagged case with no title. That made the ratchet UNSATISFIABLE BY ITS OWN DICHOTOMY on those lines -- a guard asserts nothing so it cannot honestly be tagged, and deleting it would let an operator-only LIVE-WRITE suite run unguarded, which is the exact protection DEFECT-OAG-104's AC-104.1 exists to add. The cheapest path to green was to DELETE A SAFETY GUARD, so the gate penalised precisely the discipline we want from a destructive e2e spec, and it would have recurred for every new self-guarding spec. THE POPULATION, so nobody has to re-derive it: 14 `test.skip(cond, reason)` (5 admin-app e2e credential/repair-lane guards, 9 in fids-app uc-es3/sandbox-regression) and 8 bare `test.skip()` inside test bodies (bids-board, fids-board, oi-020-reingest-contract). Every one was read individually; none was a test case. NO REAL CASE WAS EXCLUDED, and the fix asserts that in both directions: a string-first `.skip` (`it.skip('AC-ES2.6 ...', fn)`) is STILL counted, and `test.fixme`/`test.fail`/`test.slow` were ADDED to the parser's modifier set, so a TITLED pending case -- which the gate previously could not see at all -- now counts. Measured with the `--clean-tree` diagnostic the same defect added, against an IDENTICAL committed corpus of 560 files: pre-fix tool 1737, post-fix tool 1715, and no spec file changed. The same fix scores ROC 1142 -> 1136, verified read-only against that worktree, so it cannot regress the other project's loop. THE FLOOR WAS MOVED BY THE TOOL, NEVER BY HAND, and v142 auto-tighten is why it landed on the right number without anyone choosing it. The first post-fix run measured 1716, not 1715, because a co-worker's UNTRACKED `zz-oi-ac-av-11-diagnostic.scratch.test.ts` was in the working tree and contributed one violation; the floor is written from the WORKING TREE deliberately, since that is the population the gate compares every run, and writing the HEAD number against a working-tree measurement would be the same category error this defect was about. That file then went away and the next passing run tightened 1716 -> 1715 mechanically. So the committed floor now equals the `--clean-tree` HEAD measurement exactly, and the ONE-UNIT gap closed itself in minutes with no hand edit -- which is the v142 behaviour working, and the reason a transient foreign file in a shared tree is not worth blocking a floor over.
_limb2_slack_why: AC-106.6 -- THE LIMB-2 FLOOR HAS ZERO SLACK, AND THE NEXT `subprocess` STUB REGRESSES IT. Recorded 2026-08-27 rather than resolved, deliberately. limb2 sits at 15 = baseline. One of those 15 is `.claude/skills/work-items/scripts/test_work_items.py:3102`, reported as a single violation carrying TEN stub sites (the DEFECT-OAG-106 reporter said six; it is ten now, so it is still growing). The tool offers a file-level allowlist 'with the reason it asserts argv construction rather than behaviour', and MOST of those sites qualify: they assert the argv list, that no shell string is used, and that a malformed spec is NEVER EXECUTED -- and the file already drives a REAL `make` where the claim is genuinely about behaviour (`test_a_probe_that_times_out_is_broken` writes a real makefile and times out for real). NOT ALLOWLISTED, because at least two sites assert the VERDICT MAPPING against a stubbed `returncode`/`stdout` (`fake_run` returns 0 + 'BLOCKER: cleared', the test asserts `cleared`), and that is the exact founding shape of limb 2 -- `make` does not propagate a recipe's exit status, so every probe read BROKEN against real make while the stubbed mapping was green. A FILE-level exemption would silently re-open that hole to buy slack. So the disposition is: whoever next adds a `subprocess` stub anywhere in these roots will REGRESS the ratchet and must not solve it by allowlisting this file wholesale -- either split the mapping assertions onto a real binary, or take a per-site exemption with its own reason.
